problem.title: ThreadLocal Memory Leaks in Recycled Web Worker Pools
problem.prompt: Spring Boot application storing request-scoped tenant contexts and security tokens inside ThreadLocal variables.
requirements: Operational Invariant: "Any state set in a pooled worker's ThreadLocal must be deterministically cleared in a finally block before thread return."
Production Hardening: Always invoke ThreadLocal.remove() inside a mandatory try-finally block, or wrap context propagation in try-with-resources auto-closing scopes (ScopedValue in modern Java).
Prevent cascading failure by isolating downstream degradation at the ingress boundary.
constraints: Incident Scenario Baseline: Spring Boot application storing request-scoped tenant contexts and security tokens inside ThreadLocal variables.
Failure Cascade Path: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts
Sub-millisecond rejection / shed latency for overloaded requests

stages.learnerPrompt: What catastrophic failure physics occur when capacity limits or downstream dependencies degrade under peak load?

referenceMaterial.summary: Failure physics analysis: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts.
failureModes: Cascading Failure: Threads in Tomcat's worker pool are pooled and never die. Forgetting to invoke 'threadLocal.remove()' in a finally block leaves large tenant objects attached to Thread.threadLocals table indefinitely, leaking gigabytes across millions of requests.
Breakdown Chain: Burst → Pool Saturated → Queue Bloat (10k) → STW GC → 💥 504 Timeouts
Shedding Failure: Without fast rejection at the boundary, queued dead work triggers multi-second GC pauses, CPU thrashing, and cascading 504 Gateway Timeouts.
